stories.title: Scottish Premiership makes first UK move to remove Saturday 3pm broadcast blackout
summary: League to invite bids to televise all games from 2029UK leagues expected to coordinate move to end blackoutThe Scottish Premiership has made the first move in what is expected to be a coordinated attempt from the UK’s domestic leagues to remove the Saturday afternoon broadcast blackout by inviting bids to televise all of its matches in the next rights cycle from 2029.A tender document issued by the Scottish Professional Football League (SPFL) last week is understood to have given broadcasters an option to bid for live rights to all matches, including games kicking off at 3pm on Saturdays, the domestic broadcast of which is currently prohibited under Article 48 of Uefa’s statutes.

summary: Despite being at opposite ends of the table, according to Opta’s expected points model, Chelsea have performed worse than Saturday’s opponents Manchester UnitedMichael Carrick will arrive at Stamford Bridge on Saturday with the air of a dead man walking.

Yet despite Manchester United being fifth-bottom of the Premier League and Chelsea fifth-top, the Blues have performed worse this season according to Opta’s expected points model.Is there a glitch in the matrix?
